newsitem.title: USA: Snyder Oil to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: Snyder Oil to buy back shares.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp said it will probably authorize an additional $10 - $20 million of share repurchases now that its existing $30 million facility has almost expired.

Rick Wollin, vice president of corporate development, told analysts on Thursday that the company may also undertake a high-yield debt offering and use proceeds to call its convertible notes, which could represent two to three million shares if converted.
"We have 31 million shares outstanding and we want to remain in that range," Wollin said.
He said that if its convertible notes and preference shares were converted into ordinary shares this would add eight million shares to the 31 million.

John Snyder, the company's chairman, said that Snyder would make a decision on whether it would sell or completely buy Patina Oil & Gas Corp, in which it holds a 74 percent stake. "The decision will be made in the next few months on whether to buy or sell and the transaction will be complete by the end of the year," Snyder said.
